title: `podman machine start` exits 0 when API forwarding fails, so clients cannot tell the machine is unusable (Windows)
body:
## Description

On Windows, when `win-sshproxy.exe` fails to start, the machine is still reported as started successfully:

```
Starting machine "podman-machine-default"
...
API forwarding for Docker API clients is not available due to the following startup failures.
	win-sshproxy.exe failed to start, exit code: 0 (see windows event logs)

Podman clients are still able to connect.
Machine "podman-machine-default" started successfully
```

`podman machine start` exits with status 0. The warning is the only signal, and it is easy to miss when the command is invoked programmatically (Podman Desktop does exactly that). The machine is running and the CLI works over SSH, while the Docker-compatible API endpoint (`npipe:////./pipe/podman-machine-default`) does not exist.

## Root cause (confirmed via 2× deterministic repro + Windows Event Log)

**Ironclad evidence from Windows Application / .NET Runtime / Id=1000**, captured during two consecutive failed starts on 2026-11-02:

```
[error] podman-machine-default: Error occurred in execution group: error listening on socket:
        /C:/Users/x/AppData/Local/Temp/podman/podman-machine-default-api.sock:
        listen unix C:/Users/x/AppData/Local/Temp/podman/podman-machine-default-api.sock:
        bind: Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted.

[info ] podman-machine-default: Listening on: \\.\pipe\docker_engine
[info ] podman-machine-default: Listening on: \\.\pipe\podman-machine-default
```

These three events appear in every failed start, in this exact order. The execution-group semantics are **confirmed**: the AF_UNIX socket bind failure in the first entry aborts the entire group, so the two named-pipe listeners logged immediately after never actually bind. Verified by direct inspection after each failed start:

- `Get-ChildItem \\.\pipe\ | ? Name -match 'podman|docker'` → **empty** (neither pipe exists)
- `Get-Process win-sshproxy` → **nothing** (process died with the group)
- `podman images` → still lists 4 images over SSH (machine itself is up, only the Docker-compatible API path is broken)

**Trigger**: `%TEMP%\podman\podman-machine-default-api.sock` is left as a 0-byte stale file from a previous non-clean shutdown. On a clean start, podman would bind a new AF_UNIX socket here; with the stale file present, the first listener dies and takes the whole group with it.

## Steps to reproduce (verified 2×)

Observed after shutting the machine down without a clean stop. A **deterministic repro** was written and executed twice on 2026-11-02:

```powershell
# 1. Plant stale socket (mimicking non-clean shutdown)
podman machine stop
Start-Sleep 3
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:TEMP\podman" | Out-Null
New-Item -ItemType File "$env:TEMP\podman\podman-machine-default-api.sock" -Force | Out-Null

# 2. Start — expect: win-sshproxy.exe failed to start + exit code 0
podman machine start
```

Both runs produced: exit code 0, the API-forwarding warning on stderr, zero named pipes under `\\.\pipe\`, no `win-sshproxy.exe` process, and a functional `podman images` CLI (SSH-forwarded).

## Reproduction verified (2026-11-02, two full runs)

Run 1 (10:26:42–10:27:06) and Run 2 (10:28:31–10:28:58) both hit every row of this table:

| Check | Expected after start with stale sock | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$LASTEXITCODE` | 0 | ✅ 0 |
| stderr contains `API forwarding for Docker API clients is not available` | present | ✅ present |
| stderr contains `win-sshproxy.exe failed to start` | present | ✅ present |
| `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` | missing | ✅ missing |
| `\\.\pipe\podman-machine-default` | missing | ✅ missing |
| `Get-Process win-sshproxy` | nothing | ✅ nothing |
| `podman images` | lists images over SSH | ✅ 4 images |

**Fix verified** (after `Delete stale sock → stop → start`):

| Check | Expected after clean start | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stdout contains `API forwarding listening on: npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine` | present | ✅ present |
| `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` | exists | ✅ exists |
| `\\.\pipe\podman-machine-default` | exists | ✅ exists |
| `Get-Process win-sshproxy` | PID > 0 | ✅ PID=10192 |

## Expected behaviour

Either of:

- `podman machine start` returns a non-zero exit code when API forwarding could not be started, or
- the named pipes are started independently of the AF_UNIX socket, so one failed endpoint does not prevent the others.

Removing a stale socket before binding would prevent the failure altogether.

## Environment

```
podman 6.1.4 (windows/amd64, Go 1.26.8)
Windows 11 10.0.26300
podman machine (WSL2, rootless), SSH forwarding on, API socket %TEMP%\podman\podman-machine-default-api.sock
```

## Additional context

Found while investigating Podman Desktop showing empty container and image lists while the provider reported RUNNING. The inference about shared execution groups has been confirmed by two successive deterministic repro runs plus the exact 3-event sequence in the Windows .NET Runtime log.

Impact on Podman Desktop: when the machine starts half-broken but still exits 0, Podman Desktop treats it as RUNNING, discards the warning, and surfaces empty container/image lists with no error. Filed as a cross-referenced issue in `podman-desktop/podman-desktop`.

comments.body:
Quick follow-up with the **raw, unfiltered repro evidence** — all captured from two consecutive runs on 2026-11-02, both hitting every bug condition.

---

### 1. `podman machine start` stdout + stderr + exit code

```powershell
# — run 2 (the cleaner of the two) —
podman machine stop
# ...
# Plant stale socket:
# New-Item -ItemType File "$env:TEMP\podman\podman-machine-default-api.sock" -Force
# (it was already a 0-byte leftover from earlier runs)

podman machine start
Starting machine "podman-machine-default"
API forwarding for Docker API clients is not available due to the following startup failures.
	win-sshproxy.exe failed to start, exit code: 0 (see windows event logs)

Podman clients are still able to connect.
The host trusted CA certificates have been imported successfully
Machine "podman-machine-default" started successfully

$LASTEXITCODE    # → 0   ← the bug
```

After this:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem \\.\pipe\ | ? Name -match 'podman|docker'   # → empty   (BUG)
Get-Process win-sshproxy                                  # → nothing (BUG)
podman images                                             # → works!  (SSH path alive)
# REPOSITORY                       TAG
# localhost/volapi                 1.0
# docker.io/library/mysql          9
# mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk     10.0
# mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet  10.0
```

**Fix path verified** (same machine, same podman version):

```powershell
Remove-Item "$env:TEMP\podman\podman-machine-default-api.sock" -Force
podman machine stop
podman machine start
# API forwarding listening on: npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine
# Docker API clients default to this address. You do not need to set DOCKER_HOST.
# Machine "podman-machine-default" started successfully

Get-ChildItem \\.\pipe\ | ? Name -match 'podman|docker'
# docker_engine
# podman-machine-default

Get-Process win-sshproxy   # → Id=10192, ProcessName=win-sshproxy   ✓
```

---

### 2. Windows Event Log — the smoking gun

**Source**: `Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Application'; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddMinutes(-10)} | ? Message -match 'win-sshproxy|podman'`

**Key filter**: `.NET Runtime / Id=1000`, exact 3-event sequence per failed start. Both run 1 (10:26:48) and run 2 (10:28:37) produced this triplet in the same order:

```
TimeCreated          ProviderName     Id   LevelDisplayName   Message
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2026/11/2 10:28:37   .NET Runtime     1000 Error           [error] podman-machine-default:
                                                              Error occurred in execution group:
                                                              error listening on socket:
                                                              /C:/Users/x/AppData/Local/Temp/podman/
                                                              podman-machine-default-api.sock:
                                                              listen unix ...: bind: Only one usage
                                                              of each socket address
                                                              (protocol/network address/port)
                                                              is normally permitted.

2026/11/2 10:28:37   .NET Runtime     1000 Information     [info ] podman-machine-default:
                                                              Listening on: \\.\pipe\docker_engine

2026/11/2 10:28:37   .NET Runtime     1000 Information     [info ] podman-machine-default:
                                                              Listening on: \\.\pipe\podman-machine-default
```

The bind failure in the first event aborts the **entire execution group**, so the two `Listening on:` events that follow are dead on arrival. They are logged but the pipes are never created. This is why the named pipes appear fine in the event log yet don't exist on disk — and why `win-sshproxy.exe` dies with the group.

---

### Repro scripts + artifacts

Everything that produced the evidence above:

- `repro-podman-issue.ps1` — deterministic PowerShell repro with auto-checks and optional AutoFixVerify
- `artifacts/repro-20261102-102642.txt` and `repro-20261102-102831.txt` — two full raw runs (bug phase + fix phase)
- `artifacts/eventlog-20261102-102758.csv` and `eventlog-20261102-102831.csv` — raw `.NET Runtime / Application` event dumps

If the repo wants any of these uploaded, tell me where and I'll attach.

### Cross-reference + deeper root cause (Go stdlib on Windows)

After two full repro runs + tracing back to the creation timestamp of the stale `.sock` file, I found this is actually a **Go stdlib cross-platform gap on Windows**. Docker Desktop hit the same family of bugs **in August 2026** (docker/desktop-feedback#625). Posting both so maintainers have the full picture.

---

### 1. Who creates the `.sock` file, and why it never gets cleaned up

Not podman CLI. Not Podman Desktop. It's Go runtime's `net.Listen("unix", path)` inside `containers/gvisor-tap-vsock`'s `win-sshproxy`.

**Source**: [pkg/sshclient/ssh_forwarder.go · listenUnix()](https://github.com/containers/gvisor-tap-vsock/blob/main/pkg/sshclient/ssh_forwarder.go)

```go
func listenUnix(socketURI *url.URL) (net.Listener, error) {
    path := transport.UnixSocketPath(socketURI, runtime.GOOS)
    oldmask := fs.Umask(0o177)
    defer fs.Umask(oldmask)
    listener, err := net.Listen("unix", path)  // ← bare listen, no os.Remove before
    if err != nil {
        return listener, fmt.Errorf("error listening on socket: %s: %w", socketURI.Path, err)
    }
    return listener, nil
}
```

On Windows, `net.Listen("unix", path)` internally calls `WSASocket(AF_UNIX) + bind()`. The **very act of bind() creates an NTFS reparse point** with tag `IO_REPARSE_TAG_AF_UNIX = 0x80000023` on disk. That's the 0-byte file we see (`Attributes: Archive, ReparsePoint`). Go's `UnixListener.Close()` only calls `CloseHandle(h)` — it does **not** delete the reparse point from disk.

**Ironclad proof** — Go's own test code knows this:

```go
// go.dev/src/net/net_test.go
case "unix", "unixpacket":
    defer os.Remove(ln.Addr().String())   // ← test author manually cleans up!
defer ln.Close()                          // ← Close() does NOT delete on Windows
```

Why the gap? On Linux/macOS, `net.Listen("unix", path)` doesn't create a file at all — it merely *associates* a pathname with a kernel socket object. When the process dies, the socket auto-dissociates and next `bind()` at the same path usually succeeds (kernel object is gone, even if the filesystem node lingers). On Windows the semantics are flipped: `bind()` **physically creates** a reparse point on disk, but no one — not Go stdlib, not Windows OS — deletes it automatically on `Close()` or process exit.

---

### 2. The three-layer failure

| Layer | What fails | Code location |
|---|---|---|
| **Create without cleanup** | Go `UnixListener.Close()` skips reparse-point deletion on Windows | Go stdlib `net/unixsock_windows.go` (design gap) |
| **`win-sshproxy` doesn't patch it** | No `os.Remove(path)` in `SSHForward.Close()` or before `net.Listen` | `gvisor-tap-vsock` · `ssh_forwarder.go` |
| **errgroup cascades** | One failed listener kills *all* listeners in the same group, yet process still exits 0 | `win-sshproxy main.go` · `errgroup.WithContext` + `return` instead of `os.Exit(1)` |

The stale `.sock` file I traced had `CreationTime = 2026-10-31 21:33:31` — exactly the timestamp of the `.NET Runtime / Id=1000` event log triplet on that day (which was the first *successful* start that created the file, followed by an unclean shutdown that left it behind).

---

### 3. Docker Desktop hit the same family (August 2026)

Docker Desktop 4.88.1 on Windows failed to start with the same `IO_REPARSE_TAG_AF_UNIX` cleanup family of bugs, just one layer deeper:

- **Issue**: [docker/desktop-feedback#625](https://github.com/docker/desktop-feedback/issues/625) (opened Aug 26, 2026)
- **Forum thread**: [Docker Community Forums](https://forums.docker.com/t/docker-desktop-4-88-1-fails-to-start-on-windows-af-unix-socket-file-cannot-be-accessed/152314) (Aug 27, 2026)
- Docker tried `os.Remove` too, but their stale reparse points were *corrupted* (from VHDX offline compaction), so even `Remove-Item` and `fsutil reparsepoint query` couldn't touch them. Docker's fix direction is making their cleanup resilient to malformed reparse points.
- Our stale file was healthy (the socket just wasn't bound anymore), so `os.Remove(path)` before `net.Listen` should work cleanly for podman/gvisor-tap-vsock.

This suggests a **systemic issue**: any Go project using `net.Listen("unix", ...)` on Windows inherits this cleanup gap.

---

### 4. Suggested fixes (prioritized)

**Option A — in `gvisor-tap-vsock` `listenUnix()` (prevents the failure)**

```go
func listenUnix(socketURI *url.URL) (net.Listener, error) {
    path := transport.UnixSocketPath(socketURI, runtime.GOOS)
    // NEW: on Windows, clean stale reparse point before listen
    if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
        _ = os.Remove(path)  // ignore IsNotExist; log other errors
    }
    oldmask := fs.Umask(0o177)
    defer fs.Umask(oldmask)
    return net.Listen("unix", path)
}
```

**Option B — in `SSHForward.Close()` (cleans up on graceful shutdown)**

```go
func (forward *SSHForward) Close() {
    if forward.listener != nil {
        forward.listener.Close()
    }
    if forward.bastion != nil {
        forward.bastion.Close()
    }
    // NEW: if it was a unix-socket source, delete the reparse point
    if forward.sock != nil && forward.sock.Scheme == "unix" {
        _ = os.Remove(forward.sock.Path)
    }
}
```

**Option C — non-zero exit code when any listener fails** (in `main.go`)

```go
if err := group.Wait(); err != nil {
    logrus.Errorf("Error occurred in execution group: %v", err)
    os.Exit(1)  // NEW: don't just return; podman machine start needs to see the failure
}
```

Options A + C together would fix both the root cause *and* the symptom Podman Desktop sees. Option B is the "correct" "whoever creates cleans up" fix, but only protects graceful shutdowns — a hard kill still needs Option A.

Happy to help with a PR if the repo has a preferred style for this.

This makes podman basically unusable on Window, for me it started after the update to WSL 3.

Workaround: stop machine, delete corresponding .sock file in `~AppData\Local\Temp\podman`, start machine. After each boot of Windows.

will be fixed in v6.2
